classification.difficultyReason: Coefficient-ratio matching is hinted, but the task also requires matching algebraic and trigonometric roots and using a supplementary angle to identify the requested exact value.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Use the substitution $x=r\cos\theta$ and the given identity to find the value of $r$ and the trigonometric equation obtained when finding the zeroes of $P(x)$.

Hint: After substituting $x=r\cos\theta$, compare ratios with the identity.

answer.short:
$r=2\sqrt2$, so $x=2\sqrt2\cos\theta$, giving $\cos3\theta=-\dfrac1{\sqrt2}$.

Match the coefficients of $\cos^3\theta$ and $\cos\theta$ to the triple-angle identity.
answer.worked:
Take $r>0$ and substitute $x=r\cos\theta$.
$$P(r\cos\theta)=r^3\cos^3\theta-6r\cos\theta+4.$$
To match $4\cos^3\theta-3\cos\theta$, compare coefficient ratios:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{r^3}{6r}&=\frac43\\r^2&=8\\r&=2\sqrt2.\end{align*}$$
Then
$$\begin{align*}P(2\sqrt2\cos\theta)&=16\sqrt2\cos^3\theta-12\sqrt2\cos\theta+4\\P(2\sqrt2\cos\theta)&=4\sqrt2\cos3\theta+4.\end{align*}$$
Thus $P(x)=0$ becomes $\cos3\theta=-\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence, find the zeroes of $P(x)$ using two different methods to find the exact value of $\cos\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{12}\right)$.

answer.short:
Zeroes: $2,\ -1+\sqrt3,\ -1-\sqrt3$.

$\cos\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{12}\right)=\dfrac{\sqrt2-\sqrt6}{4}$.

Compare the factorised roots with the scaled cosine roots, then use $\cos(\pi-u)=-\cos u$.
answer.worked:
Algebraically, $P(2)=0$, so
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x-2)(x^2+2x-2)\\x^2+2x-2&=0\\x&=-1\pm\sqrt3.\end{align*}$$
The zeroes are $2,-1+\sqrt3,-1-\sqrt3$.

Using part (a), $\cos3\theta=-\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$. For $0\leq\theta\leq\pi$,
$$3\theta=\frac{3\pi}{4},\ \frac{5\pi}{4},\ \frac{11\pi}{4},\qquad\theta=\frac\pi4,\ \frac{5\pi}{12},\ \frac{11\pi}{12}.$$
Hence the same zeroes are
$$2\sqrt2\cos\left(\frac\pi4\right),\quad2\sqrt2\cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{12}\right),\quad2\sqrt2\cos\left(\frac{11\pi}{12}\right).$$
The second value is positive and less than $2$, so
$$\begin{align*}2\sqrt2\cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{12}\right)&=-1+\sqrt3\\\cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{12}\right)&=\frac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{4}\\\cos\left(\frac{7\pi}{12}\right)&=-\cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{12}\right)\\\cos\left(\frac{7\pi}{12}\right)&=\frac{\sqrt2-\sqrt6}{4}.\end{align*}$$
